title: Trace augmentation and kernel causal linkage protocol
author: Priya Nayar
body:
Summary:
This document defines the Trace Augmentation and Kernel Causal Linkage Protocol (TACKL): a standardized pipeline and set of annotations for enriching runtime traces so that kernel-level events, scheduler decisions, and high-level request metadata can be correlated deterministically for attribution, triage, and experiment analysis. TACKL is intended to reduce mean-time-to-detect for performance regressions, support causal attribution of tail latency to kernel events, and provide a repeatable lab protocol for validating fixes.

Scope:
- Applies to all runtime components that emit execution traces and kernel telemetry: dispatcher, scheduler, kernel plugins, KV cache, and the GPU dispatcher layer.
- Covers production sampling, deterministic augmentation in canary environments, and the lab replay pipeline.
- Not intended to replace end-to-end distributed tracing standards (Zipkin/Jaeger) but to extend them with kernel-specific causal markers and deterministic linkage.

Definitions:
- trace_id: Global request identifier propagated across layers.
- causal_span: A span annotated with a causal tag pointing to a kernel decision or event.
- kernel_anchor: A short opaque token (8-char) representing a kernel-level event group (e.g., preemption, handoff, slow-kernel).
- decision_provenance: Compact encoded tuple showing scheduler policy, priority bucket, and timestamp.

Goals and success criteria:
- Link >= 95% of sampled request traces to a kernel_anchor when a kernel event influenced latency > 5ms.
- Reduce investigation time for kernel-related tail latency incidents by 40% within 3 months of roll-out.
- Provide reproducible lab replays where kernel anchors map to the same sequence of kernel events in the sandbox.

Protocol overview:
1) Instrumentation contract:
   - All services in the runtime must propagate trace_id and include a 3-field augmentation header when emitting kernel-facing requests: kernel-anchor (nullable), decision-provenance, and preface-timestamp (RFC3339).
   - Kernel modules emit event batches to the augmentation-forwarder with fields: kernel_anchor, event_type, local_timestamp_ns, metrics={latency_ns, occupancy_pct, memory_bytes}.

2) Augmentation-forwarder responsibilities:
   - Deduplicate and fold kernel events into the canonical trace stream.
   - Attach a compact event-sig (sha1 hex truncated to 12) to the trace as causal_span.signature.
   - Promote kernel_anchor to trace-level if any event in the batch exceeds configured thresholds.

3) Sampling and retention policy:
   - Default production sampling rate: 1% of requests.
   - Tail-path selective sampling: sample all requests that enter the >99th percentile latency or hit SLA fallback paths.
   - Full diagnostic retention window for augmented traces: 30 days for incidents, 7 days for general sampling.

Trace augmentation pipeline (components and flow):
- emitter (service) -> runtime-proxy -> kernel (events) + augmentation-forwarder -> trace-assembler -> observability-store
- The forwarder runs an enrichment worker that uses a lookback table of recent scheduler decisions to attach decision_provenance to event batches.

Attribution model (heuristic + causal tagging):
- Primary attribution heuristic: when kernel_anchor exists and event latency contribution > 5ms, mark causal_span.primary = true and increment kernel_blame_score by normalized latency percent contribution.
- Secondary attribution: if multiple anchors overlap, compute weighted attribution by (kernel_event_latency * occupancy_factor) and emit a sorted list of suspected causes.
- Confidence estimate: each attribution emits a confidence tag (high|medium|low) based on event coverage and correlation score.

Experiment lab and replay protocol (step-by-step):
1) Create a deterministic replay corpus using request-surface-replay tool with URI and tokenized prompt corpus. Example CLI:
   $ ri-replay --corpus requests.jsonl --seed 42 --output replay.sig
2) Enable full trace augmentation in the sandbox cluster and set sampling=100% for the replay namespace.
3) Record kernel anchors during the run and export augmentation bundles with:
   $ augmentation-export --run-id <id> --format ndjson --output augment.ndjson
4) Validate linkage: run the causal-link-checker to ensure each trace_id in augment.ndjson maps to at most one dominant kernel_anchor.
   $ causal-link-checker augment.ndjson --threshold-ms 5
5) Compare kernel event sequences between baseline and candidate kernels using event-sig diffs and produce a report.

Investigation runbook (when you see persistent tail latency):
1) Triage: identify representative traces from the 99.9th percentile from the observability-store (filter by model, seq_len, tenant).
2) Confirm augmentation: verify trace has kernel_anchor and causal_span.signature present. If not, increase sampling for the affected route and re-run.
3) Attribution: consult the attribution table (dashboard) to see top kernel anchors and their kernel_blame_score.
4) Reproduce: run the replay protocol in a sandbox pinned to the same kernel build and scheduler policy.
5) Hypothesis & patch: use the kernel anchor mapping to propose either a scheduler param change (see table below) or a kernel fallback patch.
6) Canary: deploy patch to a canary pool with 5% traffic and augmentation sampling=100% for 1 hour. Monitor kernel_blame_score and SLO.
7) Rollback criteria: if canary SLO breach > 2x baseline or kernel_blame_score worsens by >20%, rollback immediately.

Operational controls, dashboards, and alerts:
- Dashboard widgets to create: Top kernel_anchors by blame_score, kernel_anchor time series, per-route augmentation coverage, and attribution confidence distribution.
- Alerts:
  - alert_kernel_anchor_spike: trigger when kernel_anchor frequency increases > 3x baseline in 15m window.
  - alert_unlinked_tail_traces: trigger when >30% of 99.9th percentile traces are missing kernel_anchor.
  - alert_attribution_confidence_drop: trigger when average confidence for top causes drops below 60% for 30m.
Threshold suggestions:
- anchor spike: 3x baseline for 15 minutes.
- unlinked tail traces: 30% missing link in 1 hour.

Scheduler parameter table (common knobs to try during hypothesis patching):
| parameter | range | effect | suggested safe delta |
| priority_bias | -1.0..1.0 | shifts scheduler preference between latency-sensitive and economic throughput | +/-0.1 |
| preempt_window_ms | 0..200 | window that allows cooperative preemption to occur | -10ms to +20ms |
| kv_prefetch_budget | 0..10 | number of concurrent prefetch slots per shard | +/-1 |
| evict_grace_ms | 0..500 | extra grace for soft-evictions to complete | +50ms |

Example augmentation JSON snippet emitted by augmenter (ndjson line):
{"trace_id":"t-3f7c8a","kernel_anchor":"KA9b2f1d","causal_span":{"signature":"c1a9d3b7f2aa"},"decision_provenance":"sched=v2|bucket=high|ts=2026-02-02T15:04:05Z","events":[{"type":"slow-kernel","latency_ns":8200000,"occupancy":0.86}]}

Implementation notes and safety:
- The augmentation-forwarder is a best-effort component: it must not increase request tail latency. If augmentation queue lag exceeds 100ms, the forwarder will switch to async best-effort mode and emit a telemetry event.
- Avoid storing PII in augmented traces; strip user prompt content unless requested and approved under a support ticket.
- Encryption: augmented bundles at rest must be encrypted with the default KMS key for observability assets.

Ownership and rollout plan:
- Primary owners: Runtime Observability team (owner: Priya Nayar).
- Secondary owners: Scheduler team (reviewer: Ethan Blake), Kernel team (reviewer: Mariana Soto).
- Rollout plan:
  1. Implement forwarder prototype in sandbox (Q4 2025).
  2. Internal lab validation and 100% sampling replay (Jan 2026).
  3. Canary in production with 1% sampling (Feb 2026).
  4. Full rollout with dashboards and runbook training (Mar 2026).

Appendix A — common failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing trace propagation: ensure all HTTP/gRPC libraries include trace_id header and are upgraded to runtime 3.4+. Mitigation: emergency patch to inject trace_id at proxy layer.
- Forwarder overload: backpressure to kernel emitter and fall back to async ingestion. Monitor forwarder_queue_length > 2000 as critical.
- False positive anchors: refine anchor generation by tightening event grouping windows and requiring two corroborating signals (occupancy and latency).
